identity.name: Container-Native Ransomware via Host Filesystem Escape — Cortex Cloud CDR (T1486 / T1611)
identity.summary: A container escapes to the host filesystem by parsing /proc/self/mountinfo and chroot-ing into the host root, then stages a ransomware payload. CortexSim neuters the real Ransomware-PoC clone/encrypt; the BIOC/XQL detect the chroot-escape and in-container mass-encrypt rate that Cortex Cloud CDR + XSIAM must surface.
identity.description: This scenario ports the xsiam-prisma-cdr-lab ransomware-in-container fixture into a Cortex Cloud CDR detection card. The original lab payload locates the host root mount by parsing /proc/self/mountinfo, chroot-s into it to break out of the container, installs git on the host, and clones the public Ransomware-PoC repository to detonate file-encryption on the node — a container-native variant of the host ransomware exercised by SIM-EDR-008. Because the raw payload is genuinely destructive (real host escape + a working encryptor clone), CortexSim does NOT execute it verbatim: the scenario steps reproduce the detectable telemetry shape with neutered stand-ins — a /proc/self/mountinfo read and an echo-stubbed chroot attempt, plus a bounded, reversible encrypt loop over files the scenario itself creates in a scratch directory (no host data touched, fully reverted in cleanup). The detection content is authored against that telemetry shape: a BIOC fires when a containerized process reads /proc/self/mountinfo and invokes chroot against a host-root mount (the escape primitive, T1611 Escape to Host); a second BIOC anchors the escape on the mountinfo-parse-then-chroot causality chain; and an XQL surfaces the in-container mass-file-modification rate that distinguishes a ransomware encrypt sweep from normal container I/O (T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact). A correlation rule fuses the escape and the encrypt-rate signal into one container-ransomware incident, and the reusable container-workload projection (actor_container_info JSON extraction) lets the DC attribute every event to its pod, image, and container_id. This proves Cortex covers the full container-native ransomware chain: escape to host, then impact.

actors.name: Cloud-native ransomware operators and opportunistic container intruders

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CDR-010 — container host-FS escape + neutered ransomware encrypt-rate for Cortex Cloud CDR validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM / Cortex Cloud CDR connected to the EKS cluster with the Linux agent daemonset deployed so per-container process + file telemetry reaches xdr_data.
prerequisites.check_command: kubectl -n kube-system get daemonset | grep -i cortex

prerequisites.description: cdr IaC module applied so the EKS cluster with worker nodes exists and a privileged/host-mount workload is available to exec into.

payload.code:
# NEUTERED. The original lab payload (ransomware-in-container/ransomware-poc.sh)
# performs a real chroot host escape and clones a working encryptor. CortexSim
# reproduces the DETECTABLE telemetry shape only: read /proc/self/mountinfo,
# echo-stub the chroot, and run a bounded reversible encrypt loop over files the
# scenario itself creates in a scratch dir. No host data is touched.
set -euo pipefail
HOST_FS="$(grep ' / ' /proc/self/mountinfo | awk '{print $4}' | head -1)"
echo "[CortexSim] located host-root mount candidate: ${HOST_FS:-none} — chroot escape stubbed for safety [truncated]"
WORK="$(mktemp -d /tmp/cortexsim-ransim.XXXXXX)"
for i in $(seq 1 25); do echo "benign-doc-$i" > "$WORK/file_$i.txt"; done
for f in "$WORK"/file_*.txt; do openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -salt -k cortexsim -in "$f" -out "$f.locked" 2>/dev/null && rm -f "$f"; done
echo "[CortexSim] simulated in-container encrypt sweep over ${WORK} complete — reversible, scratch-only"

input_variables.name: TARGET_NS
input_variables.description: Kubernetes namespace whose privileged/host-mount workload is exec'd into for the escape simulation.

expected_artifacts.description: A containerized process reads /proc/self/mountinfo to locate the host-root mount — the host-FS escape primitive.
chroot invoked against a host-root mount path from inside a container.
A burst of file-write/rename events as the encrypt loop produces .locked outputs and removes originals.

cleanup.code: rm -rf /tmp/cortexsim-ransim.*; echo '[CortexSim] SIM-CDR-010 cleanup complete — scratch encrypt files removed; EKS cluster owned by terraform destroy.'

iocs.context: Ransomware-PoC repository the original lab payload clones after host escape (T1486). Tracked as an IOC; CortexSim does not clone or execute it.

biocs.name: CDR-010 Container chroot to Host Filesystem Mount
biocs.description: A process inside a container invokes chroot against a host-root mount path immediately after reading /proc/self/mountinfo. This is the container-to-host escape primitive used by the ransomware-in-container payload (T1611 Escape to Host) before it detonates an encryptor on the node.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_container_info != null
| filter action_process_image_name = "chroot" or action_process_image_command_line contains "chroot"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "/host" or action_process_image_command_line contains "mountinfo"
| comp count() as escape_events by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name
| filter escape_events >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, escape_events

biocs.name: CDR-010 Host Filesystem Escape via Mountinfo Read
biocs.description: A containerized process reads /proc/self/mountinfo to enumerate the host-root mount, the reconnaissance step that anchors the chroot escape causality chain. Pairing the mountinfo read with a subsequent privileged action inside the same container distinguishes a real escape attempt from benign mount introspection.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type = ENUM.FILE_OPEN
| filter actor_container_info != null
| filter action_file_path in ("/proc/self/mountinfo", "/proc/1/mountinfo")
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("sh", "bash", "grep", "awk")
| comp count() as mountinfo_reads by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name
| filter mountinfo_reads >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, mountinfo_reads

xql_queries.name: CDR-010 Container Workload Projection
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| fields actor_container_info as container_info
| filter container_info != null
| alter pod_namespace = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.pod_namespace")
| alter pod_name = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.pod_name")
| alter image_name = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.image_name")
| alter image_id = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.image_id")
| alter container_id = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.id")
| alter privileged = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.privileged")
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("chroot", "openssl", "sh", "bash")

xql_queries.name: CDR-010 In-Container Mass File Encryption Rate
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 600)
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_WRITE, ENUM.FILE_RENAME, ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW)
| filter actor_container_info != null
| filter action_file_path contains ".locked" or actor_process_image_name in ("openssl", "gpg", "ccrypt")
| comp count() as modified_files by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name
| filter modified_files >= 10
| sort desc modified_files
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, modified_files

correlation_rules.name: Container-Native Ransomware — Host Escape Then Encrypt Impact
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(CDR-010 Container chroot to Host Filesystem Mount) AND XQL(CDR-010 In-Container Mass File Encryption Rate) — fuses the container-to-host escape with the in-container mass-encrypt rate into a single container-ransomware incident.

Cortex Cloud CDR — container escape and host-mount abuse detection

products.evidence_query: dataset = xdr_data | filter actor_container_info != null | filter action_process_image_name = "chroot" or action_file_path contains ".locked"
Correlation CR-CDR-0010 fuses the chroot host-escape BIOC and the in-container mass-encrypt-rate XQL into one container-ransomware incident.

use_cases.name: Container-Native Ransomware Detection
use_cases.description: Cortex Cloud CDR + XSIAM detect a container escaping to the host filesystem and detonating an encryption sweep — covering both the escape primitive and the ransomware impact distinct from host-only EDR ransomware.

test_cases.objective: The container-to-host escape (mountinfo read + chroot) is detected.
preconditions: cdr EKS fixture applied with the Cortex Linux agent daemonset deployed.
A privileged/host-mount workload available to exec into.
steps: Exec into the privileged workload and run the neutered escape simulation.
success_criteria: BIOC `CDR-010 Host Filesystem Escape via Mountinfo Read` fires.
BIOC `CDR-010 Container chroot to Host Filesystem Mount` fires.

test_cases.objective: The in-container encrypt sweep is detected and stitched to the escape.
preconditions: Cortex agent ingestion active so the bounded encrypt loop's file events reach xdr_data.
steps: Run the bounded reversible encrypt loop over the scratch directory.
Observe the mass-encrypt-rate XQL and CR-CDR-0010 escalate.
success_criteria: XQL `CDR-010 In-Container Mass File Encryption Rate` returns >= 1 host.
Correlation CR-CDR-0010 raises one container-ransomware incident.

preventive_controls: Run container workloads as non-root with a read-only root filesystem, drop ALL capabilities, and forbid hostPath mounts and privileged pods via admission control.
Deny the SYS_ADMIN / SYS_PTRACE capabilities and block chroot/nsenter inside workload containers with a seccomp/AppArmor profile.
Maintain immutable, versioned backups of node and persistent-volume data so an encrypt sweep is recoverable.
detection_engineering: Alert on any container process reading /proc/self/mountinfo followed by chroot against a host-root mount.
Detect an anomalous mass file-modification / rename rate inside a container (the encrypt-sweep shape).
Stitch a container escape to a subsequent impact event into a single ransomware incident.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Initial CDR container-native ransomware card for SIM-CDR-010, porting the xsiam-prisma-cdr-lab ransomware-in-container fixture. Neutered the destructive chroot escape + Ransomware-PoC clone into a detectable mountinfo-read/chroot-stub + bounded reversible encrypt loop. Authored two escape BIOCs, an in-container mass-encrypt-rate XQL, the reusable container-workload projection hunt query, IOC for the PoC repo, and correlation CR-CDR-0010. Promoted to active.
